meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'bar, pub' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Проверьте все бары и старых друзей.
examples.trans: Check all the bars and old friends.
It is already morning. Our bar is closing.

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'bartender', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Бармен, принесите нам бокал белого вина!
examples.trans: Bartender, bring us a glass of white wine!

examples.text: Бармен наливает холодную воду в стакан.
examples.trans: The bartender pours cold water into the glass.

meanings.note: Comparative: ближе. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('close, near').

examples.text: Слушайте, Марина, мы с вами стали ближе!
examples.trans: Listen, Marina, the two of us have grown closer!

meanings.note: Comparative of много. Core Russian adv meaning 'more' in everyday speech.
Comparative of большой. Core Russian adv meaning 'more' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: We need to do even more.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

бывать.gloss: to happen, to be (sometimes); to visit

meanings.en: to happen, to exist, there can be
meanings.note: 3rd person бывает = there is / can be
Часто бывать где-то. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to happen, to be (sometimes); to visit', paired with 'быть'.

examples.text: У мужчины бывает не только жена.
examples.trans: A man can have more than just a wife.

examples.text: У мужчины, мальчик, бывает не только жена. Это моя девушка.
examples.trans: A man, my boy, can have more than just a wife. She's my girlfriend.

варить.gloss: to boil, to cook, to brew

meanings.en: to boil, to cook, to brew
meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to boil', forming an aspectual pair with 'сварить'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.trans: We are cooking soup for lunch.

meanings.note: The neuter form 'всё' used alone. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
Neuter всё. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I have no idea at all.

examples.text: Я человек чистый. Я вообще не вор.
examples.trans: I'm an honest man. I'm not a thief at all.

meanings.note: Pointing at something. Core Russian part meaning 'here, there (pointing)' in everyday speech.
Emphasis. Core Russian part meaning 'here, there (pointing)' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: All right, here you go. There, look.

meanings.note: В гости = for a visit. Abstract feminine noun formed with the Slavic suffix '-ость' ('-ness, -ity') from the corresponding adjective. Common masculine noun meaning 'guest, visitor' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Клавдия Викторовна, к вам гости! Па-пам!
examples.trans: Klavdia Viktorovna, you have visitors! Ta-da!

meanings.note: давай + 1st person plural or infinitive
давай + 1st person plural or infinitive

examples.text: Давай мы его уволим, а тебя на его место назначим.
examples.trans: Let's fire him and put you in his place.

Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to do, to make', paired with 'сделать'.

examples.trans: Hi, Arkady Borisovich. What are you doing?

meanings.note: + genitive. Core Russian prep meaning 'for' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: We could open a beauty salon for you.

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: In one direction, now. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to go (on foot)', paired with 'пойти'.

meanings.note: Каждый день = every day. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('every, each').

examples.text: Аркаш, мне москвичи звонят каждый день. Может, всё-таки передумаем?
examples.trans: Arkasha, the people from Moscow call me every day. Maybe we should reconsider after all?

meanings.note: Never changes its form; masculine. Common masculine noun meaning 'coffee' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Какое хорошее утро! Лидия Алексеевна, чашку кофе, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: What a lovely morning! Lidia Alekseyevna, a cup of coffee, please.

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'coffee machine', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.trans: Do not touch the coffee machine!

examples.text: И больше никогда не трогай кофемашину!
examples.trans: And never touch the coffee machine again!

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('beautiful, pretty, handsome').

examples.text: Красивая. Но это же не ваша жена! Я вашу жену видел.
examples.trans: She's pretty. But that's not your wife! I've seen your wife.

meanings.note: в кухне / на кухне = in the kitchen, на кухню = to the kitchen
E.g. русская кухня. Entered Russian via Polish 'kuchnia' and Middle High German 'küchen', ultimately from Late Latin 'coquina' (from 'coquere', to cook).

examples.trans: And the kitchen is over there.
We are sitting in the kitchen.

examples.text: Проходите, пожалуйста! Как видите, большой коридор, а там кухня.
examples.trans: Come on in, please! As you can see, a big hall, and the kitchen is over there.

meanings.note: Agreeing, often reluctantly. Core Russian part meaning 'all right, OK' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: All right, here you go. There, look.

examples.text: А какие признаки должны быть у мастеров?

meanings.note: Usually singular only. Common neuter noun meaning 'milk' in everyday Russian.

meanings.note: + prepositional: на сайте. Core Russian prep meaning 'on, onto; for' in everyday speech.

used with не before the verb, or alone

examples.text: Я никогда не был на море.

As an adverb. Core Russian interj meaning 'bye' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Ну, покажите руки. Что у вас за спиной?
examples.trans: Well, show me your hands. What is behind your back?

meanings.note: the person helped is in the dative: 'помогать маме' = to help mum

examples.text: Так, операцию продолжаем. Михаил Михайлович, помогайте Лаврову.
examples.trans: Right, the operation goes on. Mikhail Mikhailovich, give Lavrov your help.

meanings.en: to botch, to make a mess of
meanings.note: An operation, an exam, a plan. Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'валивать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to fail, to botch', paired with 'провалить'.

Rude imperative. Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'валивать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to fail, to botch', paired with 'провалить'.

examples.trans: Just look at these Moscow types, Lieutenant. And they're the ones who mess up operations.

meanings.note: 'это просто' = it's easy. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.
Это просто = it's easy. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

meanings.note: Prefix 'раз-' ('apart, un-, thoroughly') indicates distribution or intensive action (stem 'лить'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'spill', forming an aspectual pair with 'разливать'.

examples.trans: You spilled milk on the counter.

examples.text: Ты разлил молоко на всю стойку!
examples.trans: You spilled milk all over the counter!

meanings.note: Сам, сама, само, сами. Core Russian pron meaning 'oneself (myself, yourself...)' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Я и сама хорошо проведу время.
examples.trans: I'll have a good time on my own.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'делать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to do, to make', paired with 'делать'.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.

meanings.note: Derived feminine noun formed with a productive Slavic suffix, used in spoken Russian to mean 'counter'.

meanings.note: Не трогай! = Don't touch!. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to touch', paired with 'тронуть'.

examples.text: Всё, хорошо, я тебя выпущу! Только собаку не трогай!

meanings.note: Colloquial, like здесь. Core Russian adv meaning 'here' in everyday speech.
